outline.description: This chapter establishes the context of the appeal by detailing the petitioners' background, immigration history, and the specific factual pattern used to support their asylum claims. It covers the procedural posture, including the roles of the Immigration Judge and BIA, to set the stage for the legal analysis.
subtopics: Petitioners' Profile: Surname, Origin, Immigration Status, and Cultural Context (Colombian Liberal Party Members)
Factual Foundation: Specific Incidents Constituting Alleged Persecution (Threats, Kidnapping, Property Dispute)
Procedural Posture: Jurisdiction, Compatibility of Claims (Asylum, Waiving Withholding), and Details of Administrative Orders (DJ, BIA, Court)
Evidence of the Government's Response: Police Interaction and Lack of Assistance (The 'Unwilling or Unable' Threshold)

outline.chapter_title: Governing Law and Standard of Review
outline.description: This chapter outlines the statutory and case law framework the Tenth Circuit applied. It defines the legal elements required for asylum eligibility under the INA and establishes the standard of review the appellate court applied to the Board of Immigration Appeals' findings.
subtopics: Statutory Definition of a Refugee (INA ²07(a)(A)): Protected Grounds and Fear of Persecution
The Past Persecution Presumption (8 USC § 1158(b)(1)(B)) and its Rebuttable Nature
Standard of Review for Factual Findings (Substantial Evidence) under INA § 1252(b)(4)
Scope of Judicial Review: Authority to Review BIA Decisions Despite BIA Member Composition

outline.chapter_title: Analysis of Past Persecution and Nexus to Protected Grounds
outline.description: This chapter addresses the core substantive issues of the asylum claim: whether the relied-upon incidents rose to the threshold of 'persecution' and whether they were connected to a 'political opinion' protected under the INA. The court's reasoning regarding the insufficiency of threats and the tangential nature of political motive are central here.
subtopics: Threshold of Persecution: Requirement of Harm Beyond Threats Alone (Karki, Wiransane, Ritonga)
Nature of Harm: Physical vs. Psychological Consequences and Cumulative Assessment
The Nexus Requirement: Mainstream vs. Incidental Motive (Rivera-Barrientos, Dallakoti, Yuk)
Application to Petitioners: Why 'Don Rafa' and Property Disputes Override Political Campaign Activities

outline.chapter_title: Government Protection, Safe Relocation, and Final Disposition
outline.description: This chapter concludes the opinion by analyzing the final prongs necessary for asylum: the Colombian government's actual willingness and ability to protect Petitioners, and the feasibility of safe internal relocation. It culminates in the court's holding and denial of relief.
subtopics: Government Protection Standard: 'Unable or Unwilling' Analysis (Systemic vs. Individual Evidence);
Internal Relocation Availability: Assessment of Threat Scope (Neighborhood vs. Country) and Family Ties
Symbolic vs. Realistic Threats: The Insufficiency of Hypothetical Hardship
Holding: Conclusion on Denial of Petition for Review and No Error Found
